Closest precedent: Petrov and Macdonald’s RecSys 2022 paper, *Effective and Efficient Training for Sequential Recommendation using Recency Sampling*. RSS samples target positions with probability proportional to a positive, nondecreasing recency function; its exponential form includes uniform sampling at α=1 and approaches endpoint-only prediction as α→0. Crucially, RSS removes sampled targets from the sequence and predicts them from the remaining history, potentially retaining interactions occurring after a target. It is therefore different from sampling a cutoff and predicting one target using only its preceding prefix. The original experiments applied RSS to GRU4Rec, Caser and SASRec, rather than establishing a BERT4Rec adaptation. [Original RSS paper](https://arxiv.org/html/2207.02643)

BERT4Rec already supplies another close precedent: its original paper explicitly discusses training on prefix–next-item pairs, uses random masked-item reconstruction, and adds training examples masking only the last item to better match appended-mask inference. Thus, assuming the proposal mixes endpoint targets with uniformly sampled earlier prefix targets, its ingredients have clear precedents. The meaningful distinction from RSS is prefix-only context and a single terminal masked target; the fixed endpoint probability specifies the sampling distribution. This supports describing it as a BERT4Rec sampling adaptation rather than claiming recency-biased target selection itself as novel. Whether there is additional novelty cannot be established without the proposal’s complete sampling rule and objective. [Original BERT4Rec paper, §3.6](https://arxiv.org/pdf/1904.06690)
